titles.title: Weighted Degree -- from Wolfram MathWorld

\(P_A\) is a weighted sum of monomials. It suffices to show that the expectation of every such monomial has the rational form described in Lemma 1. If this is shown, then \(\mathbb{E}[P_A]\) is a sum of such fractions: \(\mathbb{E}[P_A] = \frac{f_1(M,l)}{g_1(M,l)} + \frac{f_2(M,l)}{g_2(M,l)} + \cdots\). We put these fractions over a common denominator, obtaining \(\mathbb{E}[P_A] = \frac{f(M,l)}{g(M,l)}\) where \(g(M,l) = \mathrm{lcm}(g_1(M,l), g_2(M,l), \ldots)\). In this common denominator, \((M - (2k - 1)l)\) occurs at most \(2T/k\) times. Therefore, the degree of \(g(M,l)\) is at most \(2T \sum_{k=1}^{2T} \frac{1}{k} = O(T \log T)\). Similarly, the degree of \(f(M,l)\) is at most \(O(T \log T) + \deg g(M,l) = O(T \log T)\).
